description.full: The Menehune are a legendary race of small people in Hawaiian mythology who inhabited the Hawaiian Islands before the arrival of Polynesian settlers. Standing between two and three feet tall, these industrious beings are renowned as master craftspeople, particularly skilled in stonework, fishpond construction, and engineering. **The Menehune work only at night, completing massive construction projects in a single evening**. According to tradition, the Menehune would agree to build structures for humans, but only if the work could be completed in one night and they were fed well. If disturbed or if dawn broke before completion, they would abandon the project forever. Many ancient Hawaiian archaeological structures, including fishponds, temples, and roads, are traditionally attributed to Menehune construction.
